rationale: REFUSED, and this is the route that carries the signal this lane went looking for, which makes refusing it the uncomfortable answer rather than the easy one. The shape above is the exact structural signature of one real acquisition (acq:pump-api:aa47977575a5c7fab82dae8476b1df1a:1787369009447371-d4fc0a30381f2f0779e10a9d54ad6b35, GET /coins/search-unrestricted?limit=5&searchTerm=cat, 2026-08-22T03:22Z, HTTP 200, five rows). Bare top-level JSON array, same coin record as /coins, plus ONE FIELD THAT EXISTS NOWHERE ELSE IN THIS CATALOG: volume_1h_usd, a realised one-hour USD volume, present and non-zero on all 70 rows of every term-bearing page measured. MEASURED ORDERING: rows arrive STRICTLY DESCENDING by volume_1h_usd. Verified monotone across all 70 rows for searchTerm=cat and again for searchTerm=a, and verified to continue correctly across pages: the offset=70 page's highest volume, 1169 USD, sat below the offset=0 page's lowest, 1286 USD. It is a live-volume leaderboard filtered by a term, not a relevance ranking, whatever its path says. THE TERM IS LOAD-BEARING: with searchTerm omitted entirely, and again with it set to the empty string, the route returned long-dead coins whose volume_1h_usd was exactly 0, ordered ASCENDING by market cap. So this route cannot enumerate a global active universe in one call, and any sweep of terms that approximates one is a biased sample of whatever those terms matched. limit=100 returned 100 rows here, where the sibling /coins silently clamps to 70; two routes on one host with different silent caps, so caps are measured per route and never inherited. WHY REFUSED: identical heterogeneity to /coins. This body alone differed from a same-instant /coins page by the presence of inverted, pump_swap_pool, telegram and volume_1h_usd and the absence of profile_image and username, and none of those six is guaranteed on any row, so the whole-document fingerprint again moves with the page contents rather than with the schema. volume_1h_usd is a provider aggregate over a window whose edges this catalog cannot see, so it can never be reconciled against trades this codebase holds; it is retained as a provider assertion and nothing more. This review was made by an agent, not by Ember. It authorises nothing.
